case.claim: Demand is outrunning compute: gross run-rate rose from $9B to above $65B in seven months, and every revenue plan the record can test was met or beaten.
case.evidence: Run-rate was $9B at end-2025, above $30B on Apr 6 and above $47B in May (Anthropic, T1), then above $65B at Jul 31 (one investor update, relayed by Bloomberg, T2). Q2 recognized revenue was $11.5B, 14x YoY, 5.5% above the May projection (Bloomberg from investor documents, T3; Fortune on the leaked draft prospectus, T2; no public S-1). Q1 growth ran 80x annualized against a 10x plan (Amodei, T3). The draft says demand is 'limited principally by the availability of compute'.
case.defense: Attack: run-rate is gross and two months old, adds slowed from $13B to $7B a month, margin plans were missed (FY2025 gross margin 40% against 50%), the plan is now a selling document, and OpenAI priced Luna at a tenth of Haiku on Sep 22 (T3). Answer: Q2 recognized revenue fits the run-rate path. The model's base path needs only today's $7B a month. Q3 revenue and Haiku 5.5's price settle it.

case.claim: At Series H the model needs 47% growth a year to 2030, and the reported 2028 plan leaves only 16% a year for 2029 and 2030.
case.evidence: Model base: FY2026 $55.8B, FY2028 $195.5B (Reuters' $190B to $200B plan, T2), FY2030 $328B, DCF EV $1,189B, so Series H sits 19% below it. Reverse-DCF at base margins: Series H needs $262B of FY2030 revenue, 47% CAGR from FY2026. Series H is 14.8x end-July gross run-rate and 7.6x base FY2027 revenue.
case.defense: Attack: 47% a year for four years has almost no base rate above $25B (0.3% over three years, 0.0% over five), terminal value is 89% of EV, and FY2028 is one unverified plan. Answer: Nvidia data center grew 4.1x in two years from $47.5B and was +117% YoY in Q2 FY2027 (T1); the plan needs 3.5x from $55.8B. An analog, not proof. A 13% FY2028 miss still leaves the DCF at Series H. The haircut does not touch the DCF.

case.claim: Fixed-cost absorption has started: compute per revenue dollar fell from $1.60 to a projected $0.56, and Q2 was the first positive adjusted operating quarter.
case.evidence: Compute and infrastructure cost $7.33B on $4.59B of FY2025 revenue, $1.60 per dollar (draft prospectus via Reuters, T2; event DISPUTED for period tagging only). WSJ investor projections show $0.71 in Q1 and $0.56 in Q2 2026 (T3; scope unstated, VERIFY). Adjusted operating income was positive in Q2 and is expected positive in Q3, no dollar amount (FT, T3). The $559M figure was a May projection.
case.defense: Attack: this is absorption, not cheaper tokens; the SpaceX discount covered only the first two months; FY2025 margin missed plan by 10 points. Answer: with about 80% of compute non-cancelable, absorption is what margin expansion looks like. Base FY2026 compute plus training is 71% of revenue against about 60% in H1 (desk arithmetic), and 2028 gross margin is 64% against a 77% target (event DISPUTED). Each 5 points moves EV 14%.

case.claim: Capacity sets the pace, and at today's yield each gigawatt pays back inside its lease.
case.evidence: Gross run-rate is $28B to $46B per GW-year on 1.4 to 2.3 GW live (desk estimate, T3/T4, not company-stated). Break-even over a five-year lease is $10B on TPU-class cost and $15B at blended Q2 cost, so payback is 1.5 to 2.2 years (desk arithmetic). Colossus 1, 0.3 GW, let Anthropic double Claude Code limits within weeks (T1).
case.defense: Attack: live GW is a guess, 13.0 of 15.8 GW are 'up to', about 80% of $518B is non-cancelable, and 40% annual price deflation takes $34B per GW to $12B in two years at flat volume. Answer: the plan already embeds that fall ($12B per announced GW); the open risk is delivering 7 to 11 GW by Dec 2028. Weak as a moat: no rival capacity is in the record, and most capacity is rented.

case.claim: The enterprise base is broad and widened through the Pentagon fight.
case.evidence: Customers above $1M annualized rose from about a dozen in early 2024 to 500+ on Feb 12 and 1,000+ on Apr 6 2026 (Anthropic, T1). Eight of the Fortune 10, and over 100,000 Bedrock customers (T1; that event is DISPUTED on amounts only). Claude Code passed $2.5B run-rate by Feb 12 (T1). Menlo, an Anthropic investor, has Anthropic at 54% of enterprise coding and 40% of LLM API dollars (Dec 2025, T3).
case.defense: Attack: Amazon and Google carried 47% of FY2025 sales, two customers were 12% each, most large clients lack long-term contracts, a16z has OpenAI at 78% in production against 44%, and SpaceX bought Cursor. Answer: if each 12% customer grew only 5x in 2026, each is 5% of base FY2026 revenue (derived). Cloud partners kept Claude available under the Pentagon label (T2). Cursor still carries Claude (T4). Retention is unproven until the S-1.

case.claim: Capital efficiency is improving: equity raised is 1.9x gross run-rate, down from 4.2x at Series G.
case.evidence: PitchBook's equity-only ledger shows $124.3B through Series H ($123.4B on press and T1 sizes; VERIFY). That is 1.9x the $65B end-July run-rate, from 4.2x at Series G. FY2025 cash burn was projected at $2.8B (Fortune, Dec 2025, T2) while run-rate rose about $8B. Lenders underwrote capacity: $34.5B of lessor notes closed Jun 9 and a 17-bank $15B revolver is near final (T2; both VERIFY).
case.defense: Attack: equity-only flatters. $161.2B of leases and $518B of commitments sit outside it, the notes and revolver are obligations, and strategic money is vendor financing (Amazon: $18.0B funded, $15.0B open on delivery). Answer: I count equity only, notes once, 'up to' at zero. Commitments are 8.0x run-rate, the real gearing. About $100B of net cash (Modeler estimate) plus a reported $100B raise covers base contract payments for 2027 and 2028, $142B (Compute desk).

case.claim: Demand for the paper has exceeded supply at the last two private rounds, and OpenAI is off the 2026 calendar.
case.evidence: Series G was reported at $10B on Jan 7 and closed at $30B on Feb 12 (T2, T1). Series H was 'greatly oversubscribed' (Daniela Amodei, Jun 4, T2). OpenAI shelved a 2026 IPO and is seeking $30B privately at about $1.4T (Bloomberg, Sep 29, T3). SpaceX raised $75B, about $86B with the greenshoe, at $1.77T on Jun 12 (record and press).
case.defense: Weak as a bull argument. Attack: SpaceX fell below its $135 issue price about a month after listing on a 5% float (Wikipedia, T4, not in the record); a $100B to $130B raise is 5% to 6.5% of $2T and 1.2x to 1.5x the record; the raise is DISPUTED; IPO postponements are rising (CNBC headline, Sep 29). Answer: limited. Reported anchors (Nvidia up to $10B, T3, LOW) and longer lockups (T4) would shrink supply. Nothing is confirmed.

case.claim: The safety and trust posture has not cost the enterprise franchise, and regulated buyers co-design around it.
case.evidence: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Bank of America and Wells Fargo helped build Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (Anthropic, Sep 1, T1). Commerce approved Mythos 5 for 100+ US institutions on Jun 26 (Semafor, T2). Customers above $1M went from 500+ to 1,000+ across the Pentagon dispute (T1), and run-rate rose from $14B to $65B.
case.defense: Weak: I do not credit governance as a moat. Attack: seven founders hold 50.1% of votes on about 2% stakes (Reuters, T2; The Information, T3), the Trust has three trustees and elects 4 of 7 seats, three 2026 RSP revisions touched a capability threshold, and the D.C. Circuit upheld the Pentagon exclusion 2-1. Answer: none of that is revenue yet, and no C-suite exit is recorded in 12 months. Class A holders get economics without control (inference).

case.claim: Legal and policy losses so far are small against the run-rate, and the only fixed-dollar item is capped at $1.5B.
case.evidence: Bartz is fixed at $1.5B, final Jul 20 (T1), 0.16% of the $965B mark. Realized Pentagon loss is $150M of DoD ARR (Reuters, T2), 0.2% of the $65B run-rate. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were off for 18 days in June, revenue effect undisclosed (T1). The California federal court vacated the contractor boycott on Aug 27 (T1).
case.defense: Weak: federal action has no dollar cap. Attack: music suits carry a $5.4B statutory ceiling, the FTC probe (Sep 30, single source) and model recall are open-ended, and the Oct 21 Concord I hearing can reprice four suits. Answer: at Bartz's $3,109 per work the music suits are about $112M (desk, derived); the June recall did not stop run-rate growth ($47B in May, $65B at Jul 31).

at_price.argument: Base margins need $262B of FY2030 revenue, 47% CAGR from FY2026 (model). Base reaches $328B and a $1,189B DCF, so the price sits 19% below it; the reported 2028 plan leaves 2029 and 2030 at +16% a year. Outside view: 0.3% of firm-periods above $25B grew over 45% for three years, 0.0% for five. If base holds, the return is +24% a year over 24 months (price converging to DCF value, desk arithmetic). Bull case holds.

Base margins need $420B of FY2030 revenue (66% CAGR, past the 0.3% three-year base rate), 28% above base, or FY2028 revenue of $229B, 17% above the $195B plan; bull margins need $243B (42%). The mark is 26% above the $1,189B base DCF and 19% above about $1.26T after date roll, net cash and SBC as a cost. If base holds, the return is about 0% a year. Works only if the company beats its plan. Marks are thin (T3/T4).

Base margins need $568B of FY2030 revenue (79% CAGR, beyond the 0.0% five-year base rate), or a 49% FCF margin on base revenue (Nvidia's FY2026 GAAP operating margin is 60%, AWS 35% in 2025). Bull margins need $333B (54%), inside bull 2030 revenue of $448B, so only the bull scenario pays $2T (DCF $2,635B). If base holds, the return is -14% a year. Weakest mark for this case; I would not chase it.

outside_view.reference_class: Firms with real sales above $25B (top 1,000 by market cap, 1950-2015), plus AWS and Nvidia data center as AI-era analogs.
outside_view.base_rate: Real sales growth of 30% or more a year: 4.2% of firm-years over one year, 1.3% over three, 0.4% over five (19 of 4,472). Above 45% for five years: 1 of 4,472. Five-year median 2.0%. Year-to-year growth correlation 0.30. Nvidia data center grew +217%, +142%, +68% (FY2024 to FY2026), then +92% and +117% YoY in Q1 and Q2 FY2027. AWS grew +13% to +37% a year, +37% in Q2 2026.
outside_view.source: Record: data/model.json outside_view. Credit Suisse, The Base Rate Book (Mauboussin, Callahan, Majd), Sep 26 2016, T3, tables re-checked. Nvidia Q2 FY2027 release (Aug 26) and Amazon Q2 2026 release (Jul 30) opened by the bull analyst, T1, not in the record.
outside_view.what_is_different: Plans: no revenue plan the record can test was missed (n=5); FY2025 beat its plan 2.1x; margin plans were missed. Persistence: +1,088% in FY2025 and +1,116% in base FY2026 (H1 actual $16.2B), against a 0.30 correlation. Capacity: 15.8 GW announced against 1.4 to 2.3 GW live (T3/T4). Precedent: Nvidia grew 4.1x in two years from $47.5B; the plan needs 3.5x from $55.8B. Not different: base 56% CAGR still sits in the top bin.

thesis_breakers.threshold: Below $16.0B: run-rate flat after July. Base $17.2B, bull $17.9B, bear $16.3B (model paths; year-end $100B to $120B run-rates are projections).
thesis_breakers.current: Not reported. Q2 2026 was $11.5B recognized, 14x YoY (leaked draft via Fortune, Sep 29, T2). Run-rate above $65B at Jul 31 (Bloomberg, Aug 17, T2); nothing later is verified.

thesis_breakers.metric: Gross margin ex-training for H1 2026, and Q3 adjusted operating income
thesis_breakers.threshold: H1 gross margin below 45% (bear 2026 path; base 48%), or Q3 adjusted operating income not positive. If the S-1 gives no training split, the test is untested, not passed.
thesis_breakers.current: No GAAP figure. FY2025 about 40% (The Information, T3); Q2 2026 about 44% compute-only (PitchBook, T3); above 80% adjusted before partner share and training (FT, Sep 13, T3). Q2 adjusted operating income positive, no dollar amount.

thesis_breakers.metric: Cloud-partner fees as a share of revenue, H1 2026 (S-1 channel note)
thesis_breakers.threshold: Above 15% (FY2025 7.6%; The Information's plan implies 10.6% for 2026). Fees 5 points above the modeled level cut base EV 14% to $1,018B, 5% above Series H.
thesis_breakers.current: FY2025: $351M, 7.6% of revenue; 47% of sales via Amazon and Google at about 16 cents per dollar (Reuters on the leaked draft, Sep 29, T3). No 2026 figure.

thesis_breakers.metric: Customer concentration and retention (S-1 customer note)
thesis_breakers.threshold: Any customer above 10% of H1 2026 revenue, net revenue retention below 100%, or fewer than 1,000 customers above $1M.
thesis_breakers.current: FY2025: two unnamed customers about 12% each (Reuters, Sep 29, T2). 1,000+ customers above $1M on Apr 6 (Anthropic, T1). No retention figure is disclosed; PitchBook's 140%+ is an estimate (VERIFY).

thesis_breakers.metric: Capacity energized at Dec 31 2026, and any SpaceX 90-day notice on Colossus
thesis_breakers.threshold: Fewer than 2.0 GW confirmed online by company or partner statements, or a SpaceX termination notice after the 180-day mark (about Oct 30).
thesis_breakers.current: About 2.3 GW from T1 statements for end-2026: Amazon nearly 1 GW of Trainium, Google over 1 GW of TPUs, Colossus 1 at 0.3 GW (desk sum, may overlap held capacity). No slippage reported.

thesis_breakers.metric: Q2 2027 recognized revenue, the first full year after listing
thesis_breakers.threshold: Below $25B: closer to the bear path (about $19B) than base (about $30B). Desk arithmetic from the model's annual paths.
thesis_breakers.current: Q2 2026 was $11.5B (leaked draft, T2). The FY2028 plan of $190B to $200B (Reuters, Aug 17, T2) needs about $235B of exit run-rate in Dec 2028 (model).

concedes: At $1.5T and $2T the price needs growth almost no firm above $25B has sustained (79% CAGR at $2T), the support is the company's own plan, and about 80% of $518B of compute is non-cancelable while most large clients have no long-term contracts. A miss turns compute into a fixed charge. That asymmetry, not the growth rate alone, is the bear's best point.
disclosure: COI: the desk's model portfolio is Anthropic 6% overweight and OpenAI 2% underweight. Not cited as evidence. I red-teamed this case harder because of it, and I did not open the bear or judge files.

haircut_check.relied_on: I rely on 7.6% of revenue: platform fees of $351M on $4.59B (Reuters on the leaked draft, T3), inside PitchBook's 6% to 10% (T3). The Information's plan implies 10.6% for 2026.
haircut_check.why: It is measured and it reconciles with the FY2025 P&L. At 39.75% Q2 2026 would imply $4.6B paid to partners, against $1.9B forecast for all of 2026. And 39.75% equals 1 - (965/47)/(852/25), the haircut that ties the $965B and $852B marks at 34.1x: solved from the marks, not measured.
haircut_check.dcf_effect: None. The DCF uses gross revenue with partner fees in S&M, so net presentation moves revenue and S&M equally. If 39.75% were cash paid to partners (S&M +28.5 points), base EV would be $211B, which the fee evidence contradicts. Fees 5 points above the modeled level cut base EV 14%.
haircut_check.openai_reference: OpenAI's $852B round is 21.3x its $40B net run-rate (Bloomberg, Aug 17, T2; dates differ) and 12.2x the roughly $70B in Axios (Sep 29, T2, basis unstated). Its $1.4T ask (Bloomberg, Sep 29, T3) is 35x and 20x.
haircut_check.my_case_at_7_6: Relative value supports Series H: 16.1x net run-rate against 21.3x for OpenAI, a 25% discount, and Q2 net revenue is 1.7x OpenAI's against a 1.13x valuation ratio. At $1.5T and $2T the discount is gone.
haircut_check.my_case_at_39_75: Relative value is lost at every mark: Series H is 24.6x, a 16% premium to OpenAI, and Q2 net revenue is 1.1x OpenAI's. My case then rests on the DCF and the operating evidence, which do not depend on the haircut.
haircut_check.verdict_effect: Series H stays a bull case under both, because it rests on the DCF. $1.5T and $2T need more than relative value under either haircut. Above 15% in the S-1 fee note ends my reliance on 7.6%; a ratio near 39.75% would be the first evidence for the canonical figure.

reverse_dcf_check.method: Replicated scripts/model.py (parity with model.json on all three scenarios). Model reverse-DCF holds 2026-29 FCF at the scenario path and solves 2030 FCF. Cross-check: scale the whole growth path, training and capex with revenue, at base margins and 20x. Results match the model within 1 point of CAGR.
reverse_dcf_check.adjustments_not_in_model: Base equity value about $1,257B: date roll to Sep 30 (+8.9%), $100B net cash (Modeler estimate), SBC treated as a cost (-10.6%; the engine adds SBC back). Each is an engine limit the Modeler listed or I found; together they add about 6%.
reverse_dcf_check.return_note: Annual return over 24 months if the price converges to DCF value and value accretes at the 12% discount rate. The model EV is treated as today's value, which is conservative by about 9% (no date roll). Desk arithmetic on model outputs, not a forecast and not a probability.
